claims.text: An integrated combination of CALPHAD, first-principles calculations, and machine-learning screening can rationally identify intrinsically strong, ductile, and low-weight refractory HEA compositions.
Optimizing mixing entropy, lattice distortion, and atomic interactions produces the desired balance of strength, ductility, and low weight.
Conventionally developed tungsten-based HEAs are typically heavy and less ductile.
Integrated computational screening can select multi-principal-element combinations that favor a single-phase BCC structure.
The integrated computational approach can guide processing conditions to control grain size and balance ductility and strength.
Sputtering followed by thermal annealing is applicable to producing a refractory HEA microstructure.
Homogenization annealing under an inert atmosphere will establish a uniform microstructure in the designed alloy.
Mechanical properties should be assessed at room and elevated temperatures.
A tungsten-based refractory HEA can possess a single-phase BCC microstructure with a bimodal nanocrystalline-to-ultrafine grain-size distribution.
A beneficial grain-size distribution enhances defect recombination.
The tailored BCC microstructure provides controlled lattice distortion.
Predictions of thermodynamic stability, phase diagrams, and mechanical properties can be used to adjust elemental fractions.
Optimized lattice distortion and solid-solution strengthening beneficially regulate dislocation motion and inhibit premature failure.
Including lighter refractory elements reduces overall alloy density while maintaining high strength.
The computationally designed alloy will have significantly higher specific strength than conventional tungsten-based refractory HEAs.
The computationally designed alloy will have improved ductility while retaining or enhancing phase stability.
Conventional tungsten-based refractory HEAs exhibit strong radiation tolerance despite high density and insufficient ductility.
The design method may be limited to refractory-element compositions with similar melting points and chemical behavior.
